messages.subject: test-driven development
parts:
> On Apr 1, 2016, at 3:03 AM, wds15 <notifi...@github.com> wrote:
>
> @bob-carpenter : Just for the future: You are pointing towards test-driven development.

Or at least test-driven testing! The idea is that you put
in a so-called "regression" test (here a unit test) to make sure
the behavior doesn't go back to its old bad habits.

> For this specific case the already existing test was actually wrong. So if I were to redo this again, would it have been ok to CHANGE the existing test which tests for the wrongly transposed output to the correct behavior. That way the old test would be changed, but this would trigger the mis-behavior. Would this be ok from a test-driven dev perspective?

Yes, I think it's the only approach that makes sense.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] test-driven development
parts:
I really like The Pragmatic Programmer by Hunt and Thomas.
And the original Extreme Programming book is also good (it
was the basis of Agile, which somehow missed the original
message and turned into another process). Some people like
Steve McConnell's Code Complete, which is a bit more dry
than the other two, but still good. And there may be more
things out there since I was in the market for a book like
this as I made the move from academia to industry. For
code, I really like Martin Fowler's Refactoring book, but
it's all Java. For all the C++ template stuff, there's
Vandevoorde and Josuttis's book, which is great, and also
Alexandrescu's Modern C++ Design. These are all waiting
on C++ 11 updates, but they're way better than anything else
I've seen. Effective C++ by Scott Myers is also good; we're
not using C++11 yet, so all of the pre-C++11 versions would
be more relevant. I need to start studying up on C++!

I should put this list on our Wiki.

- Bob
